label: D1 after an unrewarded common a2->S2 trial, late in the episode (trial >= 80)
explanation: Fires only at D1, only when the reward input is 0 (previous trial unrewarded), and almost only when the previous trial was a2 with a common transition to S2 (10 of 7371 dev activations follow a1). It is also strictly late in the episode: nothing before trial ~75, rate rising through trials 80-99. All variables are observed (previous trial outcome plus the episode clock), so no future variables are used. Dev F1 0.84, mass recall 0.86. Most misses are rel -3 D1 steps, where the previous trial falls outside the window and prev_action is unknown, so the predicate cannot fire; a few are D1 after rare S1 outcomes, and a few are at trials 75-79. False positives are mostly cases where the agent goes on to switch to a1. Adding the upcoming choice (action == 2) raises precision to 0.95 but costs recall (F1 0.83), so it was left out. Activation co-occurs with a low value-head output (bottom value quantiles) and a mildly negative a1-a2 logit. It never fires at GO or D2, after rewarded trials, or after a1 choices.

issues: All the factual claims check out on dev. The feature fires only at D1 (GO and D2 have 0 of 380k steps each) and only when in_rew == 0 (never after a rewarded or penalty trial). Only 10 of 7371 activations follow a1 and 10 follow a rare a2->S1 trial (score with prev_common==0 and prev_action==2: precision 0, recall 0). Nothing fires before trial 70: dev bins 0-69 have 0 activations, 70-79 have 342, and on test, ep_trial<75 gives recall 0.002.
The scores reproduce. Dev: P 0.857 / R 0.828 / F1 0.842 / mass recall 0.864. Test: P 0.864 / R 0.821 / F1 0.842 / mass recall 0.856.

The misses are mostly structural. The rel -3 D1 steps hold 12.5% of the activation mass, and there the previous trial is outside the window, so prev_action is unknown and no predicate on it can fire. The rest are a few steps at trials 75-79 (lowering the cut to trial 75 drops dev F1 to 0.78).

The false positives are a graded weakening, not a different class of input. Precision is 0.943 when the outcome seen at the previous D1 was rewarded (the first loss after a win) and 0.745 after back-to-back losses; activation visibly decays over runs of losses. Precision is also lower at trials 80-84 (0.71) than at trials 90+ (0.905), and lower when the agent's upcoming choice is a1 (0.46, versus 0.946 for a2). Each of these is a magnitude effect within the predicate's region. None of them is a systematic counterexample.

Tried refinements: excluding repeated losses (test F1 0.823), requiring tv('action',-2) != 1 (0.834), and moving the trial cut to 78 or 82 (0.830 each). None beats the original's test F1 of 0.842. No future variables are used, and the label matches the predicate without overclaiming.
